required_sources.title: HTTP Caching (RFC 9111)
required_sources.version: RFC 9111, Standards Track, June 2022 (R. Fielding/M. Nottingham/J. Reschke, Eds.)
required_sources.locator: body lines: 581 §4.2 Freshness; 784 §4.2.4 Serving Stale Responses; 801 §4.3 Validation; 1081 §5.2 Cache-Control (5.2.1.2 max-stale request dir; 5.2.2.1 max-age response dir); 520 max-age=0 revalidation
required_sources.limits: General HTTP cache semantics; no tile/map specifics; stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error are ABSENT from this text (verified by grep) — they remain RFC 5861 extensions; no storage-size/eviction quota guidance.

required_sources.title: HTTP Cache-Control Extensions for Stale Content (RFC 5861)
required_sources.version: RFC 5861, Informational, April 2011 (M. Nottingham, Yahoo! Inc.)
required_sources.locator: TOC lines 67-70; §3 stale-while-revalidate (+3.1 example), §4 stale-if-error (+4.1 example)
required_sources.limits: Informational; defines the two extension directives only; window sizes are server-chosen values with no recommended bounds; no acquisition/resume semantics.

required_sources.title: HTTP Semantics (RFC 9110)
required_sources.locator: body lines: 3570 §8.8.3 ETag; 4799 §10.2.3 Retry-After; 5872 §13.1.2 If-None-Match; 5942 §13.1.3 If-Modified-Since; 6467 §14.2 Range; 7755 §15.5.17 416 Range Not Satisfiable
required_sources.limits: Semantics only: validators, conditional GET, byte ranges/partial content, Retry-After (single date/delay value); defines no backoff algorithm, no cache policy (see 9111), no retention bounds.
